title: EAP Hubs Receive Cultural Protection Award
content: We are very pleased to share that the EAP Hubs won the award for Cultural Protection Training Initiative at the Cultural Protection Awards organised by the International Arts and Antiquities Security Forum (IAASF). The award celebrates the people and organisations working to protect and preserve cultural heritage. Congratulations to the hub leads and the British Library staff for delivering the programme of events! Read more here.

title: Apply for an EAP grant
content:
The call for applications to EAP Round 22 is now open. Apply via the portal for projects commencing next year from July 2027. The first stage of the cycle, the Preliminary Application, is an expression of interest. Potential applicants should consult our Guide for Applicants for an overview of our requirements. The deadline for applications is Friday 6 November at midday (London time). Shortlisted applicants will be invited to submit a Detailed Application by 1 February 2027.

The webinars for applicants will be held on 15 September. Register here.

Facsimiles of the application forms can be found here.

title: Safeguarding and Digitising Historical Archives in Eastern DRC: A Regional Pilot Initiative for South Kivu and Ituri (1880-1970)
content:
This project will begin the process of safeguarding the endangered heritage of Eastern Congo by surveying fragile archives in Bunia (capital of Ituri Province) and Bukavu (capital of South Kivu Province). The collections, including parish records, community manuscripts and educational documents from the late 19th to mid‑20th century, are at risk of deterioration due to conflict, poor storage and environmental damage.

Led by ADE‑RDC, with ISP Bukavu and ISP Bunia (in collaboration with the Parish of Nyakasanza) serving as Archival Partners, the project will survey the collection of approximately 6,000-8,000 images over 3 months.

title: Preserving Indigenous Cultural and Historical Archives in Malaysian Borneo: A Pilot Study in Sabah and Sarawak
content: This Pilot project, one of the first coordinated initiatives of its kind in Malaysia, aims to survey and digitise endangered Indigenous archival materials in Sabah and Sarawak, Borneo, dating between circa 1880 and 1960. The materials, currently uncatalogued and held in private and community collections, include manuscripts, notebooks, correspondence, registers, photographs, maps, artefacts and early ethnographic documentation. Highly vulnerable due to their fragile condition, environmental exposure and lack of formal archival preservation, these items are at risk of irreversible loss. The project will prioritise high-risk and representative materials, producing high-quality digital copies to ensure long-term preservation and research access. Digitisation will support studies in history, anthropology, linguistics and Indigenous knowledge systems, whilst enabling local communities to reconnect and engage with their heritage. Beyond preservation, this pilot will establish survey strategies, metadata standards and digitisation workflows, providing a replicable framework for identifying, digitising and safeguarding other under-archived materials and at-risk collections across Malaysia and the wider Borneo region.

title: Preserving Jewish Modernism in Ukraine: Digitisation of the Cultural Archives of the Center for Judaic Studies
content:
This archive is one of the few comprehensive collections which illuminate the development of Jewish art, theatre and literature in Ukraine and beyond, ranging from the early 1900s to the mid-20th century. It includes the personal papers and correspondence of artists and writers such as Issachar-Ber Ryback, Leo Koenig, Moisei Maimon, Saul Raskin, Yosef Bergner, Boris Schatz, Marc Chagall and others who shaped modern Jewish culture.

The collection also contains documents related to the "Kultur-Lige" movement in Kyiv, Jewish political parties, and the Kyiv Jewish State Theatre (Goset). These materials provide unique insights into Jewish cultural self-organisation, modernism and the intersections of art and identity in Central and Eastern Europe.

Digitising and making this archive publicly accessible will open new perspectives for scholars studying Jewish cultural history, Yiddish literature, theatre, visual arts and music, much of which remain underexplored due to the limited accessibility of primary sources.

title: Digitisation and Preservation of Historical Documents of the Santiago Fire Brigade (1857–1913)
content:
The Santiago Fire Brigade, founded in 1863, is a distinctive Chilean institution that has operated exclusively with volunteer personnel since its establishment. Over more than 150 years, it has produced an extensive and significant body of documentation reflecting both its internal development and its direct involvement in major national events.

This project aims to digitise 5,000 documents dating from the first five decades of the institution (1857–1913), a formative period that remains poorly documented in publicly accessible archives. In addition, the project includes the conservation of 18 bound volumes through their rehousing in archival-quality boxes, as well as running training initiatives concerning the documents and programming lectures on the importance of the information they contain.

Beyond its immediate preservation objectives, the project is conceived as a fundamental step towards the establishment of a formal historical archive.

title: Digitising the surviving royal manuscripts of the Palembang Sultanate in South Sumatra, Indonesia
content: This project aims to digitise the surviving royal manuscripts of the former Palembang Sultanate in South Sumatra, Indonesia. The project will deal with 33 of the 144 volumes held by the collection. The items will be catalogued by Alan Darmawan, completing previous digitisation initiatives EAP1454 (2022) and DREAMSEA (2022). By digitising the remaining manuscripts in situ, the project will enable digital access to the whole royal collection, ultimately providing a more accurate representation of Sumatra's manuscript culture from the 17th to 19th century.

title: Digitising, cataloguing and preserving the Franciscan Archive of Salta, Argentina, from the 17th century to mid-20th century
content: This project aims to catalogue, preserve, digitise and disseminate the Archive of the Convent of San Francisco of Salta, the first religious congregation to settle in the city of Salta, from its foundation in 1582 to the present day. Recovering the hundreds of documents held in this repository is an urgent task, as they contain invaluable evidence about how the Franciscan friars conducted their missionary work during the colonial period, how they contributed to the consolidation of the Argentine state in the 19th century and how their religious, political and cultural interventions shaped the development of Salta’s society. The Franciscan apostolate was profoundly cross-sectional, serving Indigenous, enslaved and white populations alike, and involved the participation of both local actors and global networks. Digitising and making this material accessible will significantly enhance research on the region’s social, cultural and institutional history.
